summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of tracheostomy, prior cerebrovascular accident with nonverbal and immobile baseline, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and recurrent infections was admitted from a nursing home for decreased responsiveness and hypotension. He was found to be in septic shock with evidence of urosepsis, supported by purulent urine and growth of Proteus mirabilis in urine culture, though pneumonia was also considered due to new lung opacities on imaging. He was treated with fluid resuscitation, broad-spectrum antibiotics (meropenem and vancomycin), and close monitoring. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. His renal function improved, and he regained baseline mental responsiveness by discharge. Code status was updated to DNR with allowance for trach ventilation. He was discharged to extended care with plans to complete a 5-day course of IV antibiotics, monitor vancomycin levels, and hold warfarin until INR normalized.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Diabetes with neurological manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, other speech and language deficits
